new_entities.name: MTHFR-targeted methylfolate in non-deficient people
aliases: methylfolate for MTHFR variants without deficiency
new_entities.description: Use of L-methylfolate or related methylfolate supplementation in people identified by common MTHFR polymorphisms but without proven folate deficiency.

edges.effect_quant: A genotype-stratified randomized trial in 75 SSRI-resistant depression patients suggested better response to adjunctive L-methylfolate in biomarker/genotype-defined subgroups, but this was a post hoc psychiatric analysis rather than evidence that common MTHFR variants justify broad supplementation in otherwise non-deficient people. Population-level evidence mainly shows genotype-related differences in folate biochemistry, not clear consumer-facing clinical benefit.
edges.population: people with common MTHFR polymorphisms or wellness-focused MTHFR testing but without documented folate deficiency
edges.mechanism: Common MTHFR variants can modestly alter folate metabolism, but biochemical differences do not automatically create a clinically meaningful indication for methylfolate supplementation in non-deficient individuals.
edges.summary: This is a mixed and overextended claim-check edge. MTHFR genotypes can influence folate markers, and selected psychiatric subgroups may respond to adjunctive methylfolate, but that does not validate the broad wellness claim that common MTHFR variants generally require methylfolate supplementation.
edges.caveats: Do not conflate common polymorphisms with rare severe MTHFR deficiency. Much of the marketed rationale depends on genotype interpretation that exceeds the proven clinical utility of routine MTHFR testing.

evidence.citation: Papakostas GI et al 2014 J Clin Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Effect of adjunctive L-methylfolate 15 mg among inadequate responders to SSRIs in depressed patients who were stratified by biomarker levels and genotype: results from a randomized clinical trial.

evidence.citation: Hickey SE et al 2013 Genet Med
evidence.notes: ACMG Practice Guideline: lack of evidence for MTHFR polymorphism testing.

evidence.citation: Tsang BL et al 2015 Am J Clin Nutr
evidence.notes: Assessing the association between the methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) 677C>T polymorphism and blood folate concentrations: a systematic review and meta-analysis of trials and observational studies.
